title: From alto to tenor to soprano
summary: He moved from C melody to alto, then tenor after hearing Coleman Hawkins, and first played soprano in a school band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: At what point did you begin playing tenor saxophone?
I was playing tenor saxophone in Winegar's band.
Well, I'd changed to -- first I got an alto -- you mean after the C melody?
First I got an alto, and I fiddled around with that, and then I heard Coleman Hawkins, and I said, "Oh, I've got to play the tenor," and so I got myself a tenor.

And I stayed with the tenor for quite a number of years after that. In fact I used the tenor right on up, oh, until recent years, when I decided that I'd better just confine myself to alto and soprano.
When did you start playing soprano?

Believe it or not, I played the soprano in a school band, because they needed one. They had enough of the others, and although I didn't -- I always liked it, but I didn't have one, and at the time it wasn't too well thought of as an instrument, and those old sopranos, believe it or not, they were terribly treacherous. I mean the intonation was almost -- to achieve even a fair average of intonation was almost impossible.
